text:
Winnipeg is now winless in six (0-4-2), and this one never gave them a way back in. Florida scored three times in the first period, twice on the power play, with Carter Verhaeghe getting two of them. He was drafted 82nd overall by the Maple Leafs in 2013, a long way down the board from the Tkachuk brothers, who both went in the top six. The brothers did plenty here anyway: Matthew Tkachuk had four assists and Brady Tkachuk had a goal and two helpers.

The score overstates the gap in how the game was played. Florida deserved to win 60 percent of the time, meaning it took the game in 60 percent of simulated replays of every shot. At even strength, Winnipeg had the better chances (2.17 expected goals to Florida's 1.28, a measure of chance quality). The difference was special teams. Florida scored on three of five power plays, creating 1.72 expected goals with the man advantage, while Winnipeg went 0 for 2 and took twice the penalty minutes (12 to 6). Shot attempts were close, 51 for Winnipeg and 49 for Florida.

Clay Stevenson allowed 1.9 goals more than the 24 shots he faced deserved, and Akira Schmid stopped 24 of 25 for Florida, 1.57 goals better than expected. Adam Lowry's shorthanded wrap-around goal was the only thing that got past him, and it came on a 3 percent chance. Winnipeg now has to find a way to stay out of the penalty box and break a winless run that has reached six games, while Florida leaves with a 5-1 win.
